function: Digital over-the-air aggregation of federated model updates: AMP-DA at the BS estimates how many devices sent each codeword to recover the global update. pp. 5-8.
system: K=40 single-antenna devices (30% active), M-antenna BS (M=1, 4, 8), TDD uplink, complex Gaussian channel with pre-equalization; no RIS; band not stated. pp. 3-4, 9-11.
method: Federated learning (FedAvg), supervised ResNet on CIFAR-10, over a digital AirComp uplink; K-means++ learns the VQ codebook; AMP-DA is model-based, not trained. pp. 3, 7, 9.
data_channel: CIFAR-10 (50,000 train, 10,000 test images), non-i.i.d. split over 40 devices; simulated i.i.d. complex Gaussian channel; no 3GPP or measured channel. pp. 4, 9.
test_conditions: Test accuracy versus rounds reported per setting: SNR 0/5/20 dB, K=40 or 100, M=1/4/8, phase and time offsets; no train-test condition mismatch stated. pp. 9-13.
baselines: Earlier aggregation designs: OBDA [31], FSK-MV [32]. Conventional digital VQ+OFDMA (overhead only). Benchmarks: ideal FedAvg (IFed), perfect aggregation (PA). pp. 9-10.
metrics: Test accuracy versus rounds and transmitted symbols, detection NMSE, Ka estimation PMF, uplink time slots, proven O(1/sqrt(T)) convergence rate. pp. 9-12.
complexity: AMP-DA complexity of order O(I0 L N M D) per training round, equal to O(I0 L M 2^J W/Q); linear in quantization levels N. p. 8.
q1_support: p. 4: "follow a complex Gaussian distribution with zero mean and unit variance". Custom i.i.d. fading simulator; CIFAR-10 is only the learning task's dataset; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured channel.
q2_support: p. 12: "This only changes the local training dataset setting". The K=100 case is a new training run; SNR, K, M and offset cases are reported as separate results, and no model trained in one condition is tested in another.
q3_support: p. 9: "digital AirComp scheme with one-bit quantization introduced in [31]"; p. 10: "we compare the number of time slots (i.e., transmission delay), of different schemes in Table I". OBDA and FSK-MV are earlier aggregation designs; the non-learned reference is conventional VQ+OFDMA.
q4_support: p. 8: "The overall computational complexity at one FEEL training round is of the order of" O(I0 L N M D), the cost of the AMP-DA aggregation.
q5_support: p. 1: "We release our code at https://github.com/liqiao19/MD-AirComp"
notes: Area 7: the paper solves the over-the-air aggregation itself (digital AirComp, pp. 2, 13); the learned element is the FedAvg model, while AMP-DA is a model-based iterative algorithm with EM (p. 7). Flags for the reviewer: q3, the learned baselines are earlier aggregation designs OBDA and FSK-MV (p. 9) and the non-learned reference VQ+OFDMA is compared only in overhead (p. 10); q4 counts the aggregation cost (p. 8), not the model size. PDF is arXiv v2 of 29 Aug 2024 (p. 1) and prints no DOI, so the DOI was not checked against it.
